name: Park Hyatt Zanzibar
positioning: Beachfront hotel in Stone Town, set partly in Mambo Msiige, a 17th-century building, with oceanfront dining terraces and an infinity pool
best_for: Travelers who want to stay within historic Stone Town
Guests who enjoy ocean-view dining and poolside lounging

facts.text: The hotel is on a beachfront in Stone Town, a designated UNESCO Heritage site.
The hotel's address is Shangani Street in Stone Town.
The Zamani Residence includes a Library and Veranda, a Living Room and a Dining Room with an outdoor terrace.
The Pool Lounge specialises in local fish dishes alongside salads, sandwiches and snacks.
The Living Room is a setting for signature cocktails, with statement chandeliers and plush seating.
There is an Anantara Spa onsite.
There is a fitness center onsite.

highlights.text: Part of the hotel is Mambo Msiige, a historic structure built in the 17th century.
The oceanfront infinity pool overlooks Stone Town beach.
The Dining Room has the feel of a traditional Omani colonial home, with views to the dhow harbours and the Indian Ocean.
Guest rooms feature four-poster canopy beds and traditional, hand-carved Zanzibari furnishings.
All bar and dining areas have their own oceanfront terrace overlooking the beach and the Indian Ocean.

considerations.text: The hotel is in the town of Stone Town on Shangani Street, a city setting within a UNESCO Heritage site.
WhataHotel notes limited beach access due to the Stone Town location.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the luxury positioning.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: Park Hyatt Zanzibar
